jobs.title: Director of Finance And Operations
jobs.description:
About the Company

OUR VISION
Balanced relationships.
Fulfilled responsibilities.
Thriving Indigenous communities.

OUR MISSION
To create a path with our clients to community wellbeing through meaningful consulting solutions.

OUR VALUES
Relations: Everything we do is grounded in relationships and showing up in a good way.
Integrity: We deliver exceptional products and services with clarity, transparency and honesty.
Curiosity: We approach our work with curiosity, openness and genuine interest.
Culture: We respect and honour Indigenous ways of knowing and being, such as Inuit Societal Values and the Seven Grandfather teachings.
Humility: We conduct ourselves with respect, kindness and compassion.

NVision Insight Group Inc. is a majority Indigenous-owned consulting company with First Nations, Inuit, Métis and non-Indigenous shareholders, staff, associates, and subcontractors. We have extensive experience working in and with First Nation, Inuit and Métis communities and organizations, governments, corporations, and not-for-profit organizations. With offices in Ottawa, on reserve in Winnipeg, and Iqaluit, and a national team of associates, we provide a comprehensive range of high-quality consulting services across Canada.

NVision provides products and services in three practice areas.
Consulting and Advisory
Lands Studio
Learning and Development

About the Role
Position: Director of Finance & Operations
Supervisor: Board of Directors
Location: Ottawa / Iqaluit / Winnipeg / Remote

Purpose/Summary

The Director of Finance & Operations provides financial and operational leadership for NVision, helping ensure the firm is well managed, financially healthy, and positioned for long-term success. The Director establishes and implements improvements in financial processes and controls, tracking project costs, utilization, and profitability to support informed management decisions. The Director oversees financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, project costing, invoicing and cost recoveries, and profitability, working closely with colleagues to support informed decisions and the financial sustainability of the firm. The Director also leads NVision's Shared Services team, which includes finance, human resources, information technology, and administration. This involves supporting the team, strengthening internal systems and processes, and ensuring people across the firm have the support they need to do their work well. As a member of the Management Circle, the Director works collaboratively with colleagues to support the firm's direction, make thoughtful decisions about resources, and balance financial responsibility with NVision's Indigenous-led values and commitment to People, Purpose, and Profit. Alongside the Managing Director, the Director of Finance and Operations is accountable to the NVision Board of Directors.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Financial Leadership & Stewardship
Provide financial leadership and stewardship for NVision, ensuring the firm has the financial health, systems, and insight needed to support its people, purpose, and long term sustainability. Responsible to implement financial process improvements, strengthening financial systems, and leading change.
Financial policies, procedures, and internal controls: The Director carries responsibility for developing, documenting, implementing, and maintaining financial policies, procedures, and internal controls, including clearly defined responsibilities and approval authorities.
Financial reporting: The Director provides timely, accurate, accrual-based monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting, including meaningful financial analysis for management and the Board.
Lead annual budgeting, financial forecasting, and financial planning in partnership with the Managing Director and Board Finance Committee.
Oversee the firm's financial operations, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, invoicing, cash flow management, financial controls, and reporting.
Monitor financial performance, including revenue, expenses, utilization, project margins, and profitability, helping leaders understand the financial health of the firm.
Provide clear, accessible financial reporting and advice to the Management Circle and Board, supporting thoughtful decisions about growth, investments, staffing, and organizational priorities.

Project Costing & Business Performance
Strengthen project costing, pricing, and profitability practices, ensuring NVision understands the true costs and financial performance of its consulting work.
Work alongside Principal Consultants and project leaders to support effective project budgeting, resource planning, financial monitoring, and decision-making.
Develop practical tools and reporting processes that help consulting teams understand utilization, project margins, and overall performance.
Build on the findings and recommendations of NVision's external financial consultant, translating them into meaningful improvements to financial systems and practices.
Support a shared understanding of financial performance, helping leaders balance strong client relationships, meaningful work, and financial sustainability.

Shared Services Leadership & Operations
Lead and support NVision's Shared Services team, creating an environment where people have clear responsibilities, feel supported in their work, and are accountable for delivering high-quality internal services.
Oversee the firm's shared services functions, including finance, human resources, information technology, administration, facilities, and internal operational support.
Ensure internal systems, processes, and workflows support the consulting practice, making it easier for people to do their work well and serve clients effectively.
Strengthen HR practices and organizational infrastructure, including onboarding, employee support, performance management processes, policies, and compliance.
Oversee technology systems and external service providers, ensuring the firm has reliable, secure, and practical tools to support its work.
Identify opportunities to improve how the firm operates, balancing consistency and accountability with the flexibility needed in a relational, community-centred organization.
Respond to miscellaneous, non-sales or marketing email and correspondence
Complete and submitaccurate and timelytimesheets
Complete work planningand performance management processes with staff you supervise as well as for yourself

Resourcing & Organizational Sustainability
Work collaboratively with the ManagingDirector and consulting leaders to align people, capacity, and resources with the firm's priorities and anticipated work.
Support thoughtful capacityand utilization planning,helping the firm make informed decisions about staffing, recruitment, and the use of external consultants.
Connect financial planningwith business development and project delivery, ensuring growth opportunities are supported by the right resources and sustainable financial practices.
Identify emerging financialand operational risks, working with colleagues to address challenges early and find practical solutions.

Management Circle Leadership & Governance
Serve as an active member of NVision'sManagement Circle, contributing financial and operational insight to shared leadership and organizational decision-making.
Work closely with the ManagingDirector and Board Finance Committee, supporting sound financial governance, transparency, and long-term sustainability.
Bring a collaborative and constructive approach to leadership, helping colleagues understandfinancial considerations, navigatetrade-offs, and make informed decisions.
Model NVision's Indigenous-led values, ensuring financial and operational decisions reflect care for people, strong relationships, shared responsibility, and a commitment to People, Purpose, and Profit.
Participate in annualbusiness planning, strategic planning and budgeting

Qualifications

Required Knowledge, Skills, Education/Training
Indigenous identity (First Nations, Inuit, or Métis) is strongly preferred, reflecting NVision's identity as an Indigenous-led organization and the culturaland relational responsibilities of this position.
10+ years of progressive financialleadership experience, ideallywithin a professional services, consulting, or project-based organization.
Strong financial management experience and technical accounting knowledge required in financial reporting and accounting practices. Including budgeting, forecasting, cash flow, financial reporting, invoicing and cost recoveries, accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll oversight, and financial controls.
Experience establishing reliableprocesses for trackingproject costs, utilization, and profitability to support better management decisions
Demonstrated experience implementing financial process improvements, strengthening financial systems, and leading change.
Experience with projectcosting, pricing, utilization, and profitability, with an understanding of the financial dynamics of a professional services firm.
Demonstratedexperience leading and supporting teams,including responsibility for shared services or organizational operations.
Experience strengthening financialand operational systems,with the abilityto translate complex information into practical improvements.
Experience working collaboratively with senior leadership teams and Boardsof Directors.
Strong analytical, communication, and relationship-building skills,with the abilityto make financial information accessible and meaningful to others.
A relational and collaborative leadership approach, grounded in accountability, respect, and a commitment to supporting people and organizational sustainability.

Valued Indigenous Identity, Knowledge and Experience
Professional accounting designation (CPA) strongly preferred. Masters in Business Administration (MBA) is an asset. Consideration given to candidates who bring equivalent senior financial leadership experience, particularly withina professional services or consulting environment.
Experience working withinIndigenous-led organizations or alongside Indigenous communities is considered an asset.

Other Requirements
Criminal Record checkor willingness to get a criminal recordcheck.
Ability and willingness to get securityclearances as needed.

Working Conditions
This position can be basedremotely however officespace will be available in NVision physical office locations in Ottawa, Winnipeg, or Iqaluit. A reliable and fast internet connection is required.
The position will require travel.
Overtime may be required to fulfill responsibilities and meet deadlines.
The Director, Financeand Operations will be expectedto know, accept,and follow all approved NVision Insight Group Inc. policies and procedures.

jobs.description:
We are looking for a proactive, driven, highly motivated professional to join our Finance and Data Analytics teams as a Process Improvement Leader. Those showing strongest leadership, execution, and process improvement results are targeted to move into bubble assignments on key high impact projects or operational supervision roles.

You will act as a Finance SME and guide our Data & Finance teams on process improvement projects, ensuring they have proper internal controls in place and adhere to regulatory and reporting requirements.

This is a hybrid role with roughly once per month in our downtown Toronto office.

What you’ll be working on:

Leading process improvement projects working with a project team to achieve a step change in key business metrics
Supporting development of Management Systems (process controls, metrics & reporting, training, etc.)
Delivering formal and informal training with the business and new Process Improvement Leaders to train on process improvement methodology
Work Organization/Project Management: Developing and implementing plans for others, anticipating current and future needs and objectives; managing resources and ensuring tasks are completed on time and within budget
Innovation: Implementing programs that encourage, recognize, and reward innovative thinking; supports the introduction of new ideas, methods, or processes
Relationship Building: Initiating and building effective relationships with colleagues in other departments, leveraging strong interpersonal and influencing skills to support and develop effective cross-departmental relations and work initiatives

What you’ll need to have:

7+ years’ work experience in data analytics, data analysis, financial reporting, corporate accounting, controllership, FP&A, etc.
Strong understanding of IFRS, including policy research
Ability to identify control gaps and operational risks associated with finance operations and developing/implementing appropriate and effective solutions
Fast learning and clear critical thinking skills
Effective and concise communicator
Strong leadership skills
Strong self-initiative with ability to take ownership of challenges and take appropriate action
Our ideal candidate either comes straight from a large public accounting firm, or someone with a combination of public accounting and industry experience

Compensation:

The compensation for this role is $120k-150k plus 12% bonus and other benefits.

jobs.title: Sr. Director, Enterprise Finance Systems
jobs.description:
Opentext - The Information Company

OpenText is a global leader in information management, where innovation, creativity, and collaboration are the key components of our corporate culture. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to partner with the most highly regarded companies in the world, tackle complex issues, and contribute to projects that shape the future of digital transformation.

AI-First. Future-Driven. Human-Centered.

At OpenText, AI is at the heart of everything we do—powering innovation, transforming work, and empowering digital knowledge workers. We are hiring talent AI can't replace to help us shape the future of information management. Join us.

Your Impact

As Senior Director, Finance Systems within OpenText’s CDO organization, you’ll have the opportunity to shape how technology enables Finance at a global scale. This is a highly visible leadership role where you’ll lead functional and technical teams responsible for Finance systems delivery, operations, and modernization, including SAP on-premises applications and integrated services.

You’ll help drive OpenText’s Finance modernization agenda, including the implementation of S/4HANA Cloud, while partnering with senior Finance and IT leaders to turn business priorities into technology outcomes. You’ll lead through complexity, leverage AI and emerging technologies, and deliver measurable value for Finance teams and business users globally.

What You Will Do

Work closely with senior leaders to understand business objectives and develop the finance systems roadmap.
Responsible for leading the team in the delivery, operational support and continuous improvement of the SAP on-premises applications.
Finance modernization including the implementation of S/4HANA Cloud capabilities and the broader ecosystem of solutions integrated into SAP
Work with Architecture and rest of the peer network to develop and maintain Financial Systems Landscape relevance.
Accountable for delivery of change & bug-fixes for all finance Systems
Accountable for the operational upkeep of the finance systems including SOX and other IT general controls.
Accountable for people agenda for the finance systems team.
Key contributor to the overall technology delivery strategy, ensuring the realization of goals such as reuse, infrastructure simplification, cost management, solution flexibility, operational resilience and the practical use of emerging technologies, including AI, to solve outcome-driven business and IT use cases.
Build strong cross-organizational relationships and effectively influence staff across the business and IT.

What You Are Great At

Building strong relationships and effectively managing expectations with senior stakeholders, business partners, peers, and external vendors.
Breaking down complex business problems into practical technology solutions, including automation and AI, to deliver measurable business and IT outcomes.
Leading effectively in a global operating model, with teams distributed across geographies and organizational structures.
Communicating complex technical and business concepts clearly and effectively to leadership and diverse audiences.
Thinking strategically and critically, developing roadmaps, and translating strategy into execution.
Managing multiple priorities, plans, and budgets in a fast-paced environment while delivering on time and on budget.
Driving best practices, continuous improvement, knowledge sharing, and a culture of learning across teams.
Building and motivating high-performing teams and fostering an environment of trust, collaboration, and accountability.

What It Takes To Excel

10+ years of experience leading engineering, development, or technology delivery teams.
Strong experience leading complex SAP ERP delivery and operations, including SAP on-premises platforms and integrated Finance systems.
Proven experience leading S/4HANA Cloud implementations, including program delivery, business process transformation, stakeholder alignment, cutover, and post-go-live stabilization.
Strong understanding of complementary financial systems and cross-domain technology ecosystems, including Finance, HR, and CRM.
Experience supporting technology integrations related to Mergers, Acquisitions, and Divestitures (M&A).
Experience leading multiple complex workstreams within a global organization.
High-tech software or technology services industry experience is an asset.
Bachelor’s or master’s degree in a relevant discipline, college diploma, or equivalent experience.

One Last Thing:
If you’re a strategic technology leader who thrives on transformation, enjoys solving complex business challenges, and wants to shape the future of Finance technology at a global scale, we’d love to hear from you.

OpenText's commitment to diversity and inclusion surpasses legal requirements, evident in our Equal Employment Opportunity Statement of Policy which promotes a respectful and empowering environment for employees of all backgrounds, culture, national origin, race, color, gender, gender identification, sexual orientation, family status, age, veteran status, disability, religion, or other basis protected by applicable laws.

If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application or recruiting process, please submit a ticket at Ask HR. Our proactive approach fosters collaboration, innovation, and personal growth, enriching OpenText's vibrant workplace.

Compensation:
At OpenText, we offer a thoughtfully designed benefits package that supports your physical, emotional, and financial wellbeing. As you move through the hiring process, we’re happy to provide more details about our compensation programs, including variable and commission compensation opportunities for eligible roles, vacation entitlement, and paid time off.

Salary Range:
Depending on the candidate’s education, experience, skills, geographical location, and alignment with internal equity and external market, actual salary may vary and be higher or lower than the range posted.

AI Usage Disclosure:
As part of our commitment to transparency, we use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in various stages of our recruitment process, including resume screening, candidate matching, interview scheduling, and communications. These tools are designed to improve efficiency, reduce bias, and enhance candidate experience. All decisions regarding hiring are made by qualified human professionals, and we continuously monitor our AI systems to ensure fairness and compliance with applicable regulations.

jobs.title: Director, Corporate Finance & Corporate Development
jobs.description:
Director, Corporate Finance & Corporate Development

About the Company:

We are hiring for one of Canada's fastest growing technology companies, recognized by Deloitte as the #1 Enterprise Software company in the 2025 North American Technology Fast 500 and ranked #5 in Deloitte Canada's 2024 Technology Fast 50 Companies to Watch.

This is a rare opportunity for an accomplished finance leader to join a high growth Canadian technology company at a pivotal stage of its journey, with a clear path toward a future VP.
We are looking for someone who has been there before. A leader who has helped companies scale, built teams and financial infrastructure, navigated complexity and knows how to evolve a finance function as a business moves into its next chapter.

You will work closely with the CFO, CEO, and colleagues across the leadership team in a highly collaborative environment where finance is a strategic partner to the business.
This is an opportunity to help shape what comes next.

About the Role:

We are seeking a commercially minded and financially sophisticated Director of Corporate Finance & Corporate Development to support the organization’s financial strategy, corporate positioning, and potential strategic transaction opportunities.

Working directly with the CEO and CFO, this individual will help strengthen the company’s financial position, assess business value, and prepare the organization for potential sale, merger, acquisition, or strategic investment opportunities.

The ideal candidate brings experience in corporate finance, financial modelling, business valuation, transaction readiness, and stakeholder relations. This is a strategic leadership position focused on maximizing enterprise value and supporting executive-level decision-making.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Corporate Finance & Strategic Planning

Work closely with the CEO and CFO to assess the company’s financial position and long-term strategy.
Review financial performance, profitability, cash flow, and operational efficiency.
Develop financial models, forecasts, valuations, and strategic financial assessments.
Identify opportunities to improve business value and financial performance.
Provide financial insights and recommendations to executive leadership.

2. Corporate Development & Transaction Readiness

Lead corporate preparation for potential sale, merger, acquisition, or strategic investment.
Assess business valuation, enterprise value, and potential transaction structures.
Coordinate financial due diligence and organize corporate and financial documentation.
Review historical financial performance, liabilities, business risks, and growth opportunities.
Prepare confidential information memorandums, investor presentations, and transaction materials.
Coordinate with external accountants, lawyers, financial advisors, and other transaction professionals.

3. Corporate Relations & Stakeholder Management

Establish and maintain relationships with investment groups, corporate executives, financial institutions, potential acquirers, and strategic stakeholders.
Participate in strategic discussions and meetings relating to corporate transactions.
Support negotiations and evaluate potential transaction terms.
Maintain confidentiality throughout all corporate development and transaction-related activities.

4. Executive & Financial Reporting

Provide regular financial and strategic updates to the CEO and CFO.
Prepare executive-level reports, financial presentations, and valuation assessments.
Support decision-making through financial analysis and commercial insights.
Ensure financial information is accurate, organized, and transaction-ready.

5. M&A, Acquisitions & Financing

Support the evaluation of potential acquisitions, mergers, and strategic investments, from target screening through close
Build acquisition models, including standalone target valuation, merger/pro forma financials, accretion/dilution analysis, synergy estimates, and integration cost assumptions.
Perform valuation analysis using DCF, comparable companies, and precedent transactions.
Assist with financial due diligence: quality of earnings review, working capital analysis, net debt and debt-like items, and revenue and customer retention analysis.
Analyze and help structure transaction financing, including the mix of cash on hand, debt, seller notes, earn-outs, and equity issuance, and model the impact on leverage, covenants, liquidity, and returns.
Prepare materials for the executive team, board, lenders, and investors, and coordinate with legal, accounting, tax, and external advisors.
Support post-acquisition integration, including purchase price allocation inputs, consolidation into budgets and forecasts, and tracking of synergy and deal-thesis performance.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or Economics.
MBA, CFA, CPA, or other relevant financial designation considered an asset.
5–8+ years of experience in corporate finance, investment banking, M&A, transaction advisory, financial strategy, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience with financial modelling, business valuations, and due diligence.
Strong understanding of mergers, acquisitions, and corporate transaction processes.
Experience preparing businesses for investment, acquisition, or sale.
Excellent financial analysis, negotiation, and executive communication skills.
Ability to work directly with senior leadership and manage confidential financial information.
Experience with M&A transactions, due diligence, or corporate development (or investment banking or transaction advisory).
Familiarity with debt and equity financing structures, covenant modelling, and capital structure analysis.

Ideal Candidate:

The successful candidate is strategic, analytical, commercially aware, and comfortable operating at an executive level. They understand how businesses are evaluated by potential buyers and investors and can identify opportunities to strengthen financial performance and maximize enterprise value.

This individual must be comfortable working in a dynamic environment, taking ownership of strategic financial initiatives, and advising executive leadership on important corporate decisions.

What We Offer:

Direct exposure to executive leadership and strategic decision-making.
An opportunity to influence corporate strategy and business valuation.
A collaborative, growth-oriented working environment.
Competitive compensation based on experience.

Director

Full-time

Industries

IT Services and IT Consulting and Computer and Network Security

We are seeking a commercially minded and financially sophisticated Director of Corporate Finance & Corporate Development to support the organization’s financial strategy, corporate positioning, and potential strategic transaction opportunities.

Working directly with the CEO and CFO, this individual will help strengthen the company’s financial position, assess business value, and prepare the organization for potential sale, merger, acquisition, or strategic investment opportunities.

The ideal candidate brings experience in corporate finance, financial modelling, business valuation, transaction readiness, and stakeholder relations. This is a strategic leadership position focused on maximizing enterprise value and supporting executive-level decision-making.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Corporate Finance & Strategic Planning

Work closely with the CEO and CFO to assess the company’s financial position and long-term strategy.
Review financial performance, profitability, cash flow, and operational efficiency.
Develop financial models, forecasts, valuations, and strategic financial assessments.
Identify opportunities to improve business value and financial performance.
Provide financial insights and recommendations to executive leadership.

2. Corporate Development & Transaction Readiness

Lead corporate preparation for potential sale, merger, acquisition, or strategic investment.
Assess business valuation, enterprise value, and potential transaction structures.
Coordinate financial due diligence and organize corporate and financial documentation.
Review historical financial performance, liabilities, business risks, and growth opportunities.
Prepare confidential information memorandums, investor presentations, and transaction materials.
Coordinate with external accountants, lawyers, financial advisors, and other transaction professionals.

3. Corporate Relations & Stakeholder Management

Establish and maintain relationships with investment groups, corporate executives, financial institutions, potential acquirers, and strategic stakeholders.
Participate in strategic discussions and meetings relating to corporate transactions.
Support negotiations and evaluate potential transaction terms.
Maintain confidentiality throughout all corporate development and transaction-related activities.

4. Executive & Financial Reporting

Provide regular financial and strategic updates to the CEO and CFO.
Prepare executive-level reports, financial presentations, and valuation assessments.
Support decision-making through financial analysis and commercial insights.
Ensure financial information is accurate, organized, and transaction-ready.

5. M&A, Acquisitions & Financing

Support the evaluation of potential acquisitions, mergers, and strategic investments, from target screening through close
Build acquisition models, including standalone target valuation, merger/pro forma financials, accretion/dilution analysis, synergy estimates, and integration cost assumptions.
Perform valuation analysis using DCF, comparable companies, and precedent transactions.
Assist with financial due diligence: quality of earnings review, working capital analysis, net debt and debt-like items, and revenue and customer retention analysis.
Analyze and help structure transaction financing, including the mix of cash on hand, debt, seller notes, earn-outs, and equity issuance, and model the impact on leverage, covenants, liquidity, and returns.
Prepare materials for the executive team, board, lenders, and investors, and coordinate with legal, accounting, tax, and external advisors.
Support post-acquisition integration, including purchase price allocation inputs, consolidation into budgets and forecasts, and tracking of synergy and deal-thesis performance.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or Economics.
MBA, CFA, CPA, or other relevant financial designation considered an asset.
5–8+ years of experience in corporate finance, investment banking, M&A, transaction advisory, financial strategy, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience with financial modelling, business valuations, and due diligence.
Strong understanding of mergers, acquisitions, and corporate transaction processes.
Experience preparing businesses for investment, acquisition, or sale.
Excellent financial analysis, negotiation, and executive communication skills.
Ability to work directly with senior leadership and manage confidential financial information.
Experience with M&A transactions, due diligence, or corporate development (or investment banking or transaction advisory).
Familiarity with debt and equity financing structures, covenant modelling, and capital structure analysis.

Ideal Candidate:

The successful candidate is strategic, analytical, commercially aware, and comfortable operating at an executive level. They understand how businesses are evaluated by potential buyers and investors and can identify opportunities to strengthen financial performance and maximize enterprise value.

This individual must be comfortable working in a dynamic environment, taking ownership of strategic financial initiatives, and advising executive leadership on important corporate decisions.

What We Offer:

Direct exposure to executive leadership and strategic decision-making.
An opportunity to influence corporate strategy and business valuation.
A collaborative, growth-oriented working environment.
Competitive compensation based on experience.
